verses.text: I thought about all this and explored it all: the righteous and the wise, and what they do, are in God's hand. No one knows whether love or hate is waiting for them. Everything lies ahead of them.

The same thing comes to everyone. The same end comes to the righteous and the wicked, to the good, to the clean and the unclean, to those who offer sacrifices and those who do not. As it is with the good person, so it is with the sinner. As it is with those who make promises, so it is with those who are afraid to make them.

This is the evil in everything that is done under the sun: the same end comes to everyone. Also, people's hearts are full of evil, and there is madness in their hearts while they live. After that, they join the dead.
Whoever is still among the living has hope. Yes, a living dog is better than a dead lion.
For the living know they will die, but the dead know nothing. They have no more reward, and even the memory of them is forgotten.
Their love, their hate, and their jealousy have long since disappeared. They will never again have a part in anything that happens under the sun.
Go, eat your bread with joy, and drink your wine with a happy heart, for God has already approved what you do.
Always wear white clothes, and always put oil on your head.

Enjoy life with the wife you love, all the days of this meaningless life that God has given you under the sun, all your meaningless days. For this is your reward in life and in the hard work you do under the sun.
Whatever your hand finds to do, do it with all your strength. For in the grave, where you are going, there is no work, no planning, no knowledge, and no wisdom.

I looked again and saw under the sun that the race is not won by the fastest, nor the battle by the strongest. Food does not always come to the wise, nor riches to the clever, nor favor to the skilled. Time and chance happen to them all.
For no one knows when their time will come. Like fish caught in a cruel net, and like birds caught in a trap, so people are caught by evil times that fall on them suddenly.
I also saw this example of wisdom under the sun, and it impressed me greatly.
There was a small city with only a few people in it. A powerful king came against it, surrounded it, and built great siege works against it.
Now a poor but wise man lived there, and by his wisdom he saved the city. Yet no one remembered that poor man.
So I said, "Wisdom is better than strength." But the poor man's wisdom is looked down on, and no one listens to his words.
The quiet words of the wise are better than the shouting of a ruler among fools.
Wisdom is better than weapons of war, but one sinner can destroy much good.
